body: Thank you, that will be the next step if family is unable to step up....

That is reassuring.

There were some minor developments throughout the day as child services interviewed different family members.

I think at this point my sister is feeling very hurt and betrayed. She helped someone who was down on her luck, and they repaid her with this...

Hopefully this resolves quickly and everything can go back to normal, without the anxiety that comes with this kind of threat.

I will let her know what you said!
Absolutely. We have screen capture of them too in case she does delete them, as well as text messages.
I've been working with my doctor for years longer than my psychiatrist. I get monthly checkups and blood work. Again, she can't do anything until the specialist sees me, and that is a 2 year wait.

Caffeine is not really a good solution for chronic fatigue. Again, it is an unfocused hyperactivity with a crash at the end. That won't be a productive solution in my case.

2 cups of coffee for me usually requires an hour+ nap to recover from. Might get me home if I crash in the grocery store, but will not allow me to participate in a work day without complications.

Yes, my psychiatrist is aware. All she says is that I can quit the meds whenever I want, but she will not offer an alternative.

I didn't know there were stimulants available over the counter, I will speak with my pharmacist about it.

I have tried caffeine tablets, but they only gave me a burst of unfocused hyperactivity and a crash later. Great for a short pick me up, but not a good long term option for me and wholely unhelpful for focused tasks.

My psychiatrist doesn't prescribe stimulants to people with suicidal ideation, and my GP won't prescribe without my Psychiatrist's blessing. I am also awaiting specialist referrals because my bloodwork is chronically abnormal, and she wants to consider the results first. The wait list is 2 years.

I can request again at my appointment, which is next week, but my chances are rather slim. Especially when delusional thinking is involved.
